evidence.exact_quote: The primary Assistant mode strip exposes five stable choices: `Ask`, `Agent`, `Debug`, `Plan`, and `Deep Plan`.

items.impact: Builders and consumers have a closed, stable primary workflow vocabulary instead of inventing additional Assistant modes.
items.statement: The primary mode strip is explicitly closed to Ask, Agent, Debug, Plan, and Deep Plan, with specialized workflows normalized as overlays rather than replacements.
items.title: Primary Assistant mode vocabulary is closed

evidence.exact_quote: - Before any mutation-capable step after `target_binding`, the assistant MUST revalidate the investigation when the target identity, bound worktree/branch, requested/effective runtime identity, auth/account binding, or instrumentation availability has drifted.
- `verification` is not optional. A fix attempt without a recorded verification result remains `attention_required` or `failed_cleanup`, not `resolved`.

items.impact: Mutation after target drift is gated, and a debug run cannot claim resolution without recorded verification and cleanup semantics.
items.statement: Debug Mode defines a closed phase model with mandatory revalidation before drifted mutation and a falsifiable resolution oracle requiring verification.
items.title: Debug resolution is gated by revalidation and verification

evidence.exact_quote: - Stop first records `chat_run.cancel_requested`, sends cancel to the active model/tool/subagent leases, waits up to `cancel_grace_ms = 3000`, and then records `chat_run.cancelled` or `chat_run.cancel_timeout` before queued messages may advance.

items.impact: A timed-out lease could emit late output or mutations while a queued message begins, creating transcript corruption, duplicate work, or cross-run side effects.
items.statement: The Stop contract names `chat_run.cancel_timeout` but does not define whether the queue advances after timeout, how late lease results are quarantined, or what recovery state owns still-running model, tool, or subagent work.
items.title: Cancel timeout lacks late-effect containment

evidence.exact_quote: - **Persistence:** Mode is a per-session or per-chat setting (configurable in chat UI or settings). `for session` does not persist across app restarts; durable approval/default behavior is owned by `Plans/Permissions_System.md`.

items.impact: Different implementations may restore YOLO or Regular posture at different scopes, producing unsafe or misleading authority after thread switches or application restart.
items.statement: The phrase `per-session or per-chat` leaves the persistence owner and precedence of execution mode unresolved, especially when chat state, app settings, and durable approval defaults disagree.
items.title: Execution-mode persistence scope is unresolved

evidence.exact_quote: - `user` scope persists as a user-level preference only when the content is not project-confidential
- Teach MUST NOT persist secrets, tokens, passwords, or other credentials

items.impact: Durable taught behavior is bounded by explicit confirmation, scope, confidentiality, and credential exclusions.
items.statement: Teach defines explicit persistence scopes and prohibits credential storage, while user-level persistence is conditioned on content not being project-confidential.
items.title: Teach persistence has explicit scope and secret boundaries

evidence.exact_quote: - browser capture chips stay pending, visible, and removable until the user sends; `cmd.browser.add_selection_to_chat` creates a `browser_selection_context` chip, `cmd.browser.pick_element_for_chat` creates a `browser_element_context` chip, and neither command auto-sends a chat message

items.impact: Browser-derived context cannot silently enter a model turn and remains inspectable and removable before send.
items.statement: Browser capture is explicitly represented as visible pending chips with separate selection and element types and no auto-send behavior.
items.title: Browser capture remains visible and user-controlled

evidence.exact_quote: - The multi-question lifecycle is `draft → incomplete → ready_to_submit → submitted → paused`: `draft → incomplete` when the user begins answering, `incomplete → ready_to_submit` when all `required` questions are answered, `ready_to_submit → submitted` when the user confirms submit, and `paused` when the user dismisses without submitting.
flow_state: "draft" | "incomplete" | "ready_to_submit" | "submitted" | "paused" | "dismissed" | "timed_out" | "unavailable";

items.impact: Implementations may treat dismissal as a transition after submission, as `paused`, or as `dismissed`, causing incompatible outputs, resume behavior, and draft retention.
items.statement: The prose lifecycle orders `submitted → paused` while simultaneously saying pause occurs on dismissal without submission, and the canonical envelope adds separate `dismissed`, `timed_out`, and `unavailable` flow states without transitions.
items.title: Questionnaire lifecycle contradicts its canonical enum

evidence.exact_quote: These are deterministic first-implementation budgets. They are ceilings/defaults, not promises that every planning run must use the full budget.

| Deep Plan | Balanced | 6 | deep local research across relevant subsystems, constraints, and prior docs | multi-source cited web research when helpful | full markdown plan doc + TODO list + risks + alternatives + validation notes |

items.impact: Two conforming implementations can make materially different research and questioning decisions while both claiming the same PT level, weakening predictable UX and acceptance tests.
items.statement: The PT matrix gives numeric question ceilings but leaves research breadth and web activation to phrases such as `when helpful`, without observable trigger thresholds or minimum work needed to distinguish adjacent PT levels.
items.title: Plan Thoroughness research triggers are subjective

evidence.exact_quote: - TODO items include `order_index` and `notes`; `order_index` owns item-level ordering, while `notes` carry reviewer or execution context without changing status.

- Legacy tool payloads `todos: Array<{ id?, content, status? }>` and `todos: Array<{ id, content, status }>` normalize into the Assistant TODO schema with `todo_id`, `title`, `summary`, `dependencies[]`, `owner_hint`, and `verification_hint`; `TODO` remains the visible checklist concept, not a second schema.

items.impact: Planning, tool, persistence, and GUI consumers share one ordered TODO representation with an explicit legacy normalization boundary.
items.statement: The normalized TODO contract owns item ordering, notes, status semantics, and legacy tool-payload normalization without minting a second checklist schema.
items.title: TODO projection has a single normalized contract

evidence.exact_quote: - Recovery is anchored by `revision_run.{bundle_id}.{revision_id}`. Interrupted runs preserve `revision_id`, `resumed_from_revision_id?`, `interrupted_at`, safe-point metadata, and per-annotation history; already-validated annotation outcomes remain persisted through resume/retry.

items.impact: Interrupted targeted revisions have stable identity, safe points, and persisted per-annotation outcomes for deterministic resume or retry.
items.statement: Annotation revision recovery preserves revision lineage and validated outcomes rather than replaying the entire run without identity.
items.title: Targeted revision recovery preserves safe-point lineage

evidence.exact_quote: - Execution starts only after explicit approval and uses `regular` or `yolo`, never `plan`.

items.impact: Plan outputs cannot silently mutate project files or execute under a read-only planning posture.
items.statement: The planning-to-execution handoff has a direct oracle: explicit approval is mandatory and the follow-on runtime posture must be regular or explicitly selected yolo, never plan.
items.title: Plan execution requires explicit approval

evidence.exact_quote: - **Deterministic budget caps:** Auto-retrieval has strict per-source limits (queries/hits/bytes) so it cannot crowd out user/assistant messages.

items.impact: Context pressure, latency, and retrieval cost remain implementation-dependent, and tests cannot prove that retrieval stayed within a canonical budget.
items.statement: Auto-retrieval requires deterministic per-source query, hit, and byte caps but supplies no values, derivation rule, configuration owner, or observable cap-hit behavior beyond truncation notes.
items.title: Auto-retrieval budget caps have no values

evidence.exact_quote: | `suspended` | `active` | `cmd.chat.thread.restore` | Restores transcript, metadata, and restorable UI state; ephemeral stream/queue state is not restored. |
- `active`: keep the full transcript, queue state, thread metadata, runtime references, and restorable UI state

items.impact: A restored thread could either lose or rehydrate queued work depending on whether `queue state` is interpreted as durable active-state data or ephemeral restore-excluded data.
items.statement: The lifecycle contract says active threads keep queue state while restore explicitly excludes ephemeral queue state, but it does not distinguish durable queue metadata from transient queued content or define the suspension transition cleanup.
items.title: Thread restore leaves queue persistence boundary unclear

evidence.exact_quote: - `resolved`, `cancelled`, and `superseded` investigations reopen as historical views by default; they do not silently restart automation, instrumentation, or browser/dev sessions.

- `failed` pairs with `stop_reason_code = investigation.verification_failed`, `investigation.no_repro_observed`, `investigation.budget_exhausted`, `investigation.runtime_unavailable`, `investigation.target_unreachable`, or `investigation.adapter_unavailable`.

items.impact: Failed investigations cannot be restored, displayed, classified as terminal, or superseded deterministically even though runtime stop reasons map to that state.
items.statement: The final-state mapping emits `failed`, but reopen semantics enumerate only resolved, cancelled, and superseded terminal histories and provide no failed-state lifecycle or recovery rule.
items.title: Failed investigation state has no lifecycle semantics

evidence.exact_quote: - `attention_required` investigations do not auto-resume execution; reopen restores the Investigation Context with the current `attention_required_reason_code` and allowed recovery actions.
- `attention_reason_code?`

items.impact: Storage, restore, and GUI consumers may serialize different keys, causing the recovery reason or allowed actions to disappear after reopen.
items.statement: Reopen semantics require `attention_required_reason_code`, while the canonical Investigation Context header imports `attention_reason_code?`; no alias or migration rule reconciles them.
items.title: Attention reason field names conflict

evidence.exact_quote: - `Raw` shows an accordion list of messages; expanding a message exposes the full serialized payload for that message, plus related `tool-part` payloads, provider metadata blobs, and path/runtime data needed for debugging
- truncation, redaction, and context-serialization state remain visible per item; the UI MUST NOT silently present omitted context as if it were still serialized

items.impact: Full provider, tool, path, and runtime payloads may disclose credentials, sensitive paths, or data beyond the viewer's authority despite visible redaction-state labeling.
items.statement: The Raw pane promises full serialized payloads but does not define viewer authorization, field-level secret scrubbing, reveal consent, export behavior, or retention limits; displaying redaction state does not itself specify what must be redacted.
items.title: Raw Context Detail lacks an access and scrubbing contract

evidence.exact_quote: - The inline operation-card family explicitly EXCLUDES question cards, permission-request approval cards, the sticky plan-tracker panel, reasoning-transparency blocks, and delegated-task or subagent disclosure blocks; those are separate widget families and require an explicit design decision before becoming operation-card variants.

items.impact: GUI consumers cannot collapse semantically different question, approval, plan, reasoning, and delegated-task widgets into the lifecycle-bearing operation-card state model.
items.statement: The operation-card family has an explicit ownership and exclusion boundary for command, web/search, and diff/edit lifecycle artifacts.
items.title: Operation-card exclusions prevent widget-family conflation

evidence.exact_quote: - The Firecrawl owner section must either preserve `changeTracking` with its structured output shape or explicitly retire it as out of scope; same URL change tracking requires a previous fetch in cache/storage and returns `change_status: "new" | "same" | "changed" | "removed"` in output rather than disappearing silently.

items.impact: Builders cannot know whether change tracking is required, and downstream schemas, cache retention, GUI disclosure, and acceptance tests cannot be finalized.
items.statement: The canonical text leaves Firecrawl `changeTracking` as an either-preserve-or-retire branch instead of deciding the product capability and migration outcome.
items.title: Firecrawl change tracking remains an open product branch

evidence.exact_quote: - single confirmation prompt showing all unique domains in the batch
- For Session grants all listed domains for that session

items.impact: A user may be forced to grant every domain or abandon the batch, and an implementation may retain broader session authority than intended without a canonical partial-grant outcome.
items.statement: The batch permission rule grants all listed domains after one prompt but does not define deselection, partial approval, denial of one domain, grant revocation, or how the batch proceeds when only a subset is authorized.
items.title: Batch domain approval has no partial-grant semantics

segments.summary: Reviewed primary modes, planning and Debug overlays, runtime normalization, provider/model controls, ELI5, permissions, message controls, queueing, slash commands, and web routing; found unresolved permission persistence and cancel-timeout containment while confirming closed mode and debug verification contracts.

Reviewed Git/GitHub routing, dispatcher parity, Teach, attachment and browser context, web provenance, questionnaires, and Plan Thoroughness through Deep Plan artifact rules; found a contradictory questionnaire state model and non-falsifiable PT research triggers.

Reviewed TODO normalization, annotation and targeted-revision behavior, plan approval and execution handoff, file/source-control boundaries, search and retrieval, chat taxonomy, and thread identity/lifecycle; found unquantified retrieval caps and an unclear queue persistence boundary.

Reviewed investigation reopen and final states, routing and runtime identity, branching, context usage and Investigation Context, operation cards, web activity/provenance, and batch domain permission context; found unmodeled failed investigations, conflicting attention fields, missing raw-view privacy controls, unresolved change tracking, and incomplete partial-grant semantics.
